backup.restore_point: PENDING - name the backup set taken immediately before this apply
backup.production_rule: Expand only: one new function public.guest_booking_status_v1(text) (security definer, empty search_path, execute for service_role only) and one index on guest_access_tokens(booking_id). No data change; guest_access_tokens has 0 rows today. restore_point and verified_at (epoch) are placeholders: take a fresh backup, re-read the clock, then fill both (fill-restore-point.mjs does it). Take a fresh backup if the one named is more than an hour old at apply time.

forward_verification.name: function_exists_definer_empty_search_path
forward_verification.query: select count(*) = 1 and bool_and(p.prosecdef and p.proconfig = array['search_path=""']) from pg_proc p where p.pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace and p.proname = 'guest_booking_status_v1'

forward_verification.name: grants_service_role_only_anon_authenticated_and_public_none
forward_verification.query: select has_function_privilege('service_role','public.guest_booking_status_v1(text)','execute') and not has_function_privilege('anon','public.guest_booking_status_v1(text)','execute') and not has_function_privilege('authenticated','public.guest_booking_status_v1(text)','execute') and not exists (select 1 from pg_proc p, aclexplode(p.proacl) a where p.oid = 'public.guest_booking_status_v1(text)'::regprocedure and a.grantee = 0)

forward_verification.name: booking_id_index_exists
forward_verification.query: select count(*) = 1 from pg_indexes where schemaname = 'public' and tablename = 'guest_access_tokens' and indexname = 'guest_access_tokens_booking_id_idx'

steps.name: run_compensating_script
steps.action: Apply supabase/rollbacks/20261006_booking_status_tokens.sql with run-sql-on-host.sh: it drops the function and the index. Issued tokens stay in guest_access_tokens. Roll back the stay-site (stay.html and the Track your booking link) and the guest-access and submit-booking functions too.

feature_flags.name: sql_then_functions_then_site
feature_flags.required_state: Apply this release BEFORE deploying guest-access (its view=status branch calls the RPC), then submit-booking (mints the token and returns status_url), then publish stay-site. The old guest-access ignores view=status and keeps answering the guide request, so an out-of-order deploy fails safe: the page shows the neutral "We could not load your booking just now" retry message (a 200 reply with no status), never a booking and never an endless Loading.

compatibility.rehearsal: PENDING - run pgTAP booking_status_tokens (24 tests) and the rollback body on a restored backup before apply. Expected on a --no-acl restore (B103): the 4 grant assertions (anon, authenticated, service_role and PUBLIC execute, tests 2-5) fail by design because that backup cannot carry grants; the CI database job proves them. Do not weaken the suite.
compatibility.evidence: Production read-only (2026-10-06): booking_inquiries.status holds pending, confirmed, cancelled (no CHECK) and expire_booking_holds_v1 writes expired; service_role has no grant on booking_holds, which is why the hold deadline is read through a definer function; guest_access_tokens has only its pkey and token_hash unique index, RLS on, service_role grants only. Old guest-access and submit-booking callers are unaffected: the function and index are new.

stop_conditions: any forward verification query returns anything other than its expected value
the restore point is older than one hour
restore_point or verified_at is still empty or still the PENDING placeholder
the rehearsal has not run the pgTAP suite green on this commit
guest-access is deployed before this release is applied
